clue.text: Members bound to keep to themselves, even?

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all for yourself
scores that are even are tied

explanation.surface: A club whose members are expected to keep themselves to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' are limbs here, not people in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog-tied animal has its legs strapped together, so its limbs are literally fastened up.

clue.text: In Ancient Greek, no end of grammar

indicators.note: 'no' says the following letter is to be left out of the poet's name

parts.note: the epic poet of the Iliad and Odyssey

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is meant

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A remark about how Greek grammar seems to go on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' reads as 'endless', but it means 'without the end of grammar', the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in, staying at their house rather than out, is said to be at home.

clue.text: Lady jockey in the news, almost always

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for always is dropped

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: the word for jockey sits inside the other letters

parts.note: to jockey for position is to vie or compete

explanation.surface: A female jockey who never seems to be out of the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' is a verb meaning compete, not a rider. 'the news' is gen, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevieve is a woman's given name, here clued simply as a lady.

clue.text: No half measures from lowdown artist, female, and lowdown artist-poet

parts.note: the lowdown is the inside information

explanation.surface: A painter and a poet who commit fully to everything they do.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is built as INFO-RA-PENNY then INFO-RA-POUND; RA is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that once committed to a small stake you may as well commit wholly, so it urges total commitment.

clue.text: Spanker, maybe, was made to pull up bloomers

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up turns the letters to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a spanker is a fore-and-aft sail on the aftermost mast
someone who had to do something was made to do it

explanation.surface: Someone who spanks being forced to hitch up a pair of knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are old-fashioned knickers in the surface, but here they are plants that bloom. A spanker is a sail on a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are garden flowers, and flowering plants can playfully be called bloomers.

clue.text: Gradually, Post Office couple refusing to serve grasping pensioner

indicators.note: grasping means holding on to something, so one pair of letters closes round another

parts.note: a pair of conscientious objectors, people who refuse military service

explanation.surface: Two post office workers who won't serve an elderly customer and get hold of him.
explanation.walkthrough: A conscientious objector refuses to serve in the armed forces; only the first of the pair does the grasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Poco a poco is the Italian musical direction meaning little by little, that is bit by bit.

clue.text: One doing handouts allowed in chap to feed baby

indicators.note: the word for allowed sits inside the word for chap

parts.note: to baby someone is to pamper them

indicators.note: feeding puts something into a mouth, so this group goes inside the outer word

explanation.surface: A man permitted to feed an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is the verb meaning spoil, not the infant; LET goes into HE, and that whole goes into PAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphleteer writes and distributes pamphlets, the leaflets handed out to the public.

clue.text: Nice area where young retire in western Europe: endless astonishment

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for astonishment is cut off

parts.note: a baby's bed, where an infant goes to sleep

clue.text: Dish when warm emits aromas at the outset

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: emitting sends something out, so that letter leaves the word for warm
the outset is the start, so only the opening letter of aromas counts

explanation.walkthrough: An ashet is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashet is a large oval platter for serving meat, so a type of dish.

clue.text: Switch positions with English girl: promotion wasted

parts.note: a switch can be set to off or on

clue.text: It's a gas using axes to slice melon!

the x and y axes of a graph

clue.text: Undergarment picked up for revel

clue.text: Issue pack that's easily handled

clue.text: Out-of-tune shepherd-tenor would ruin opera

explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus in the Underworld is Offenbach's comic operetta, the source of the famous can-can.

clue.text: Groom footballer for award?

clue.text: Smart men dressed down — one found in bed?

clue.text: After skirmishing ok — the rest on stretchers

explanation.surface: Wounded soldiers resting on stretchers after a minor battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The stretchers are not for casualties: tenterhooks hold cloth taut on a drying frame.

clue.text: With this tweet, mean to be heard?

parts.note: mean in the sense of stingy

clue.text: Native of Channel Islands, note, descending on Japanese school

clue.text: See tailless sloth's burying its head in squalor

clue.text: Skimpy attire Keith gingerly covers up

covering something hides it, so the answer lies concealed in these words

parts.note: the hidden run inside these words

clue.text: A month from Quebec to the Alaskan port
